title: Introduction to Computer Science
description: Introduction to the intellectual enterprises of computer science and the art of programming. This course teaches students how to think algorithmically and solve problems efficiently. Topics include abstraction, algorithms, data structures, encapsulation, resource management, security, and the Chrome V8 engine. Languages include C, Python, SQL, JavaScript, CSS, and HTML.

title: Data Structures and Algorithms
description: Design and analysis of algorithms. Topics include divide and conquer, dynamic programming, greedy algorithms, graph algorithms, network flow, NP-completeness, and approximation algorithms. Also covers fundamental data structures: heaps, hash tables, balanced binary trees, and union-find.

title: Machine Learning
description: Supervised and unsupervised learning from a unified probabilistic perspective. Topics include linear and logistic regression, support vector machines, neural networks, clustering, dimensionality reduction, and Bayesian methods. Emphasis on both understanding the methods and applying them to real-world data.

title: Operating Systems
description: Principles and practice of operating system design and implementation. Topics include processes and threads, synchronization, memory management, file systems, I/O, and security. Students implement core OS components in a series of programming projects.

title: Systems Programming and Machine Organization
description: Introduction to systems programming and computer organization. Topics include C and assembly programming, memory management, system calls, linking, and the memory hierarchy. Students develop a deep understanding of how software interacts with hardware.

title: Algorithms for Big Data
description: Algorithms for processing data that is too large to fit in memory. Topics include streaming algorithms, sketching, dimensionality reduction, locality-sensitive hashing, external memory algorithms, and MapReduce-style computation. Emphasis on both theory and practical applications.

title: Multivariable Calculus
description: Calculus of functions of several variables, vector analysis, and applications. Topics include vectors and matrices, partial derivatives, multiple integrals, line and surface integrals, and the theorems of Green, Stokes, and Gauss.

title: Linear Algebra and Differential Equations
description: Matrices, linear transformations, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, and ordinary differential equations. Topics include Gaussian elimination, vector spaces, inner products, and applications to physics and engineering.

title: Studies in Algebra and Group Theory
description: A rigorous treatment of linear algebra and abstract algebra for students with strong mathematical backgrounds. Topics include groups, rings, fields, modules, and representation theory. Considered one of the most challenging undergraduate mathematics courses in the US.

title: Analysis I: Complex Function Theory
description: Complex numbers, holomorphic functions, Cauchy's theorem, Taylor and Laurent series, the residue theorem, conformal mappings, and applications. Emphasis on rigorous proofs and conceptual understanding.

title: Intermediate Microeconomics
description: Consumer and producer theory, competitive markets, monopoly, oligopoly, game theory, and market failures. Introduces formal economic modeling and welfare analysis. Essential preparation for advanced courses in economics.

title: Intermediate Macroeconomics
description: National income accounting, growth theory, business cycle models, monetary and fiscal policy. Topics include Solow and endogenous growth models, IS-LM and AS-AD frameworks, and open economy macroeconomics.

title: Microeconomic Theory
description: Graduate-level treatment of consumer and producer theory, general equilibrium, social choice, and mechanism design. Covers duality theory, game theory, and information economics with mathematical rigor.

title: Introduction to Probability
description: A focused introduction to probability. Topics include sample spaces, conditional probability, Bayes' theorem, random variables, distributions, expectation, variance, the law of large numbers, and the central limit theorem. Famous for its elegant and intuitive approach.

title: Linear Models
description: Theory and application of linear regression. Topics include simple and multiple regression, model diagnostics, variable selection, analysis of variance, and logistic regression. Extensive use of R for data analysis.

title: Probability Theory
description: Graduate-level probability. Measure-theoretic probability, sigma-algebras, random variables, integration, convergence theorems, characteristic functions, central limit theorems, martingales, and Brownian motion.

title: The World Since 1945
description: A global history of the postwar world. Covers decolonization, the Cold War, the emergence of the Third World, globalization, and the end of the Cold War. Emphasis on the intersections of political, economic, and cultural history.

title: American Democracy: A History
description: Traces the history of American democracy from the colonial era to the present. Topics include the founding documents, the expansion of suffrage, the Civil War, Reconstruction, the Progressive Era, the New Deal, civil rights, and contemporary challenges to democracy.

title: Introduction to Psychological Science
description: An introduction to the scientific study of mind and behavior. Topics include neuroscience, perception, learning and memory, language, intelligence, emotion, development, personality, social psychology, and mental health.

title: Social Psychology
description: An examination of how people think about, influence, and relate to one another. Topics include attitudes, persuasion, conformity, obedience, group dynamics, prejudice, aggression, and prosocial behavior.

title: Genetics and Genomics
description: Molecular and classical genetics, genome structure and function, gene expression and regulation, recombinant DNA technology, and genomic approaches to biology. Explores how genetic information is encoded, transmitted, and expressed.

title: Evolutionary Biology
description: Evolution by natural selection, adaptation, speciation, phylogenetics, and macroevolution. Topics include population genetics, kin selection, sexual selection, and the evolution of development.

title: Principles of Organic Chemistry
description: Structure, bonding, reactivity, and synthesis of organic compounds. Topics include stereochemistry, nucleophilic substitution, elimination reactions, carbonyl chemistry, and spectroscopic methods of structure determination.

title: Organic Chemistry II
description: Continuation of CHEM 17. Topics include conjugated systems, aromatic chemistry, amines, carbohydrates, amino acids, and natural product synthesis. Emphasis on multi-step synthesis and retrosynthetic analysis.

title: Ethical Reasoning
description: An introduction to moral philosophy and its application to contemporary issues. Topics include consequentialism, deontology, virtue ethics, and their application to questions about justice, equality, human rights, and the good life.

title: Philosophy of Mind
description: The nature of mind and consciousness. Topics include the mind-body problem, functionalism, physicalism, qualia, intentionality, and the computational theory of mind. Engages with both classical texts and contemporary debates.

title: Introduction to Comparative Politics
description: A systematic introduction to the study of political regimes, institutions, and behavior around the world. Topics include democratization, authoritarianism, elections, political parties, and the political economy of development.

title: Classical Political Philosophy
description: An introduction to political philosophy through close reading of foundational texts by Plato, Aristotle, Machiavelli, Hobbes, Locke, Rousseau, and Kant. Topics include justice, authority, liberty, and the best form of government.

title: Data Science in Politics
description: Application of modern data science methods to political science questions. Topics include causal inference, survey experiments, text analysis, machine learning for social science, and computational social science.

title: Economics and Computation
description: The intersection of economics and computer science. Topics include mechanism design, auction theory, market design, algorithmic game theory, and computational social choice.

title: Neuroscience of Behavior
description: An introduction to the neural basis of behavior. Topics include the structure and function of neurons, synaptic transmission, sensory systems, motor control, learning and memory, emotion, and mental disorders.

title: Introduction to Electrical Engineering
description: Fundamentals of electrical engineering. Topics include circuit analysis, signal processing, linear systems, digital logic, and microprocessors. Lab sessions provide hands-on experience with electronic components and measurement tools.

title: Introduction to Applied Mathematics
description: Mathematical methods for science and engineering. Topics include linear algebra, differential equations, Fourier analysis, probability, and numerical methods. Emphasis on formulating and solving real-world problems.

title: Human Evolutionary Biology
description: The evolutionary biology of the human species. Topics include primate evolution, the fossil record of human origins, behavioral ecology, genetics of human populations, and the evolution of modern human diversity.
